classification: derived classical GR model; not experimental evidence
domain: r>=r0>0; two asymptotically flat sides; proper l∈R; code r0∈[0.001,1e9] m, 1<=r/r0<=1000
derivation: b(r0)=r0, b'(r0)=-1<1; redshift Phi(r)=0, no horizon from lapse
Einstein orthonormal components: epsilon=(c4/8piG)b'/r²; p_r=-(c4/8piG)b/r³; p_t=(c4/8piG)(b-rb')/(2r³)
Independent proper radial R(l)=sqrt(l²+r0²): G_(tt)=(1-R'²-2RR'')/R², G_(ll)=(R'²-1)/R², G_(theta theta)=R''/R
For b=r0²/r: epsilon=p_r=-c4*r0²/(8pi G r4); p_t=+c4*r0²/(8pi G r4), epsilon+p_r<0, epsilon+p_t=0
Ricci scalar R=-2r0²/r4, locally finite at throat; model does not check global stability
validation: domain, signature, throat and flare-out unit tests
shape derivative vs central finite differences
Einstein orthonormal stress equations in shape and proper radial coordinates
anisotropic stress conservation via numerical pressure derivative
radial NEC and tangential NEC sign tests
independent JavaScript implementation and Node tests
limitations: Chosen curve and supporting stress-energy are postulated within classical general relativity. They are not an observed wormhole, do not demonstrate material capable of sourcing this stress, and do not establish stability, traversability under perturbations, quantum energy inequality compatibility or backwards time travel. No claim of a general quantum energy inequality bound follows from a local energy density.
